sources.title: Coulomb stable structures of charged dust particles in a dynamical trap at atmospheric pressure in air
sources.notes: Reported operating RF examples include 2 kV at 80 Hz with 900 V end DC; 4.4 kV is a simulated parameter in the paper, not the displayed operating experiment. Charges in ordered structures are estimates from gravity balance.

sources.title: Dust Particles Behavior in an Electrodynamic Trap
sources.source_class: peer-reviewed primary experiment and Brownian-dynamics model
sources.notes: The separate CTPP paper reports an experimental four-rod linear Paul trap at 50 Hz, Uω=4400 V AC amplitude in the paper's sinusoidal convention, and Uend=900 V DC; Al2O3 radius 10–15 µm, density 0.38×10^4 kg/m^3, estimated charge about 10^5–5×10^5 e. Rods were 3 mm diameter and 12 cm long, axis spacing 1.3 cm, end-electrode gap 6.5 cm. The paper does not fully specify in the accessible text whether Uω is a terminal-to-ground or differential pair amplitude; do not convert it to RMS or peak-to-peak. This is not the same operating point/geometry as the NJP paper's displayed 2 kV, 80 Hz example; its 4.4 kV also appears as a numerical-model input in the NJP article.

sources.title: Measurement of the charge of a single dust particle
sources.notes: Abstract reports separate mass and charge ranges; individual paired values must be extracted from the full text before drawing correlations.

sources.title: The charging of microparticles in corona discharge in the air
sources.venue: Herald of Dagestan State University, Natural Sciences 31(4) (2016)
sources.notes: Reports measured individual Al2O3 sizes and charges after corona charging; charging voltage is on the corona charger, not the trap.

sources.title: Microparticle separation in a linear Paul trap
sources.notes: Open-air separation experiment of corona-charged glassy carbon and alumina; reported model charges are not all direct single-particle measurements.

sources.title: Multipole Electrodynamic Ion Trap Geometries for Microparticle Confinement under Standard Ambient Temperature and Pressure Conditions
sources.notes: Experimental 8- and 12-electrode traps, multiparticle structures in air; does not report counter-rotating orbits.

sources.title: 3M Glass Bubbles K, S and iM Series Technical Data Sheet
sources.notes: K20 true density 0.20 g/cm3; particle-size distribution d10/d50/d90 30/60/90 micrometers; crush-strength data are distributional and do not imply electrical performance.

sources.title: 3M Glass Bubbles K, S and iM Series Technical Data Sheet
sources.notes: K1 true density 0.125 g/cm3 (0.10-0.14); d10/d50/d90 30/65/115 micrometers and effective top size 120 micrometers. Isostatic test pressure 250 psi, target fractional survival 90%, minimum 80%. Product mechanical specification only, not electrical strength or charge data.

sources.title: A linear Paul trap to study the equilibrium of charged micron-sized particles in air
sources.source_class: preprint; not independently peer reviewed as of 2026-11-20
sources.notes: Uses 3M K-series hollow-core spheres, diameter 80-120 micrometers, at 50 Hz and 1 bar; charge is triboelectric. Reports q=(1.16±0.08)e6 e, q/m=(3.8±0.5)e-4 C/kg, and derived m=(4.9±0.7)e-10 kg. The same paper gives a manufacturer-density estimate 6.5e-11 kg for 100 micrometers, about 7.5 times lower; these estimates are not jointly measured and must remain separate.

sources.title: A charged-particle manipulator utilizing a co-axial tube electrodynamic trap with an integrated camera
sources.notes: Coaxial tubes, ambient-air trapping, 300-750 V amplitude, 30-140 Hz, particle diameters 3-50 micrometers.

sources.title: The Transition to Paschen's Law for Microscale Gas Breakdown at Subatmospheric Pressure
sources.notes: Characterizes field-emission/Townsend transition for 1-25 micrometer gaps; classical Paschen use is not universal at microscale.

sources.title: Gas breakdown in atmospheric pressure microgaps with a surface protrusion on the cathode
sources.notes: Demonstrates strong sensitivity of atmospheric microgap breakdown to cathode-protrusion geometry; DC study, not a direct low-frequency RF threshold.

sources.title: DC and RF Breakdown in Microscale Gaps from near vacuum to atmospheric pressures
sources.venue: U.S. Department of Energy technical report (2022)
sources.source_class: government technical report with experimental and modeling work
sources.notes: Studies RF and DC breakdown across pressures and microscale gaps; frequencies and gaps differ substantially from the present 10^2 Hz, submillimeter geometry.
